body:
### Summary

When a project has `dynamic = ["version"]` and `[tool.uv] package = false`, uv still installs setuptools and calls `get_requires_for_build_wheel` to get the version. The project is never built. uv writes it to `uv.lock` as `source = { virtual = "." }` with no version, so the result isn't used.

This breaks projects with a flat layout. Setuptools rejects them during package discovery, so `uv lock` fails:

```toml
[project]
name = "example"
dynamic = ["version"]
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = []

[tool.uv]
package = false
```

```console
$ mkdir foo bar && touch foo/__init__.py bar/__init__.py
$ uv lock
error: Failed to build `example @ file:///.../example`
  cause: The build backend returned an error
  cause: Call to `setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__.get_requires_for_build_wheel` failed (exit status: 1)

         [stderr]
         error: Multiple top-level packages discovered in a flat-layout: ['foo', 'bar'].
```

Without the two folders, `uv lock` succeeds. `uv lock -v` still shows uv installing setuptools and calling the backend.

If `uv.lock` already lists the project without a version, `uv lock --locked`, `uv sync --locked` and `uv run` work. `uv lock --upgrade`, `uv lock --upgrade-package <name>` and `uv add` call the backend again and fail.

I expected uv to skip the build backend for a project with `package = false`, because it doesn't need a version for that project. #10689 fixed this for the case where the lock file can be reused, but not for a new resolve.

My use is an application that's never built or published. I'd like to leave the version out, but the spec requires `version` or `dynamic` in `[project]` (see #10522). `dynamic = ["version"]` would be the right way to say it, if uv didn't run the backend.

### Platform

macOS 27.0 arm64

### Version

uv 0.13.5 (Homebrew 2026-10-22 aarch64-apple-darwin)

### Python version

Python 3.13.13
title: Dynamic version runs the build backend for a project with `package = false`
